description: Use before concluding that a generated artifact is missing, that a pipeline/job stalled, or that a step "never ran" — and before proposing to clear state, delete a marker, or re-run to produce it. Trigger when the evidence is "there is no <expected-name> file".
anchors: A pipeline wrote output files named from a heading the model chose. Looked for the name I expected, did not find it, reported the run as stalled and proposed clearing its completion marker. The artifact was there under a different name.
note: Operator label: "ambigiouse" — whether a missing expected filename means the artifact is absent depends on the writer, so the lesson is the question to ask, not a verdict.

description: Use when writing file, note, or source references into a document a human will read — an outline, spec, deck sketch, research write-up, README, or citation list. Guides choosing a link form that resolves where that document gets read.
anchors: Wrote citations as [label](~/path/to/file.md) in a research write-up. Tilde paths resolve in no editor, no Obsidian, no GitHub. The document was read in two places with different base paths.
note: Operator label: global.

description: Use when explaining, documenting, comparing, or slide-writing about an external method, pattern, tool, or someone else's workflow — and the user's own repo, harness, or notes already define a vocabulary for that kind of thing.
anchors: Wrote a deck section about someone else's interview loop using three headings invented on the spot, while the user's own skill-build references already defined flow / loop state / stop criteria for that kind of thing.
note: Operator label: "good global skill" — overruled a project recommendation. The named artifacts are illustrations; the habit holds wherever the user keeps a taxonomy.

description: Use when a task needs facts about an external idea, author, talk, tool, paper, or method and the reflex is to web search. Check the user's local notes vault first, then fan the remaining questions out to parallel agents.
anchors: Went straight to web search for facts about an author the user had already written literature notes on. The user keeps a zettelkasten at ~/obsidian/Z-Core; the notes were there, in the user's own words, with onward links.
note: Operator label: global, machine-scoped — "vault can be not exist, should be parametrized somehow". Body must name the anchor and the fallback when absent.

description: Use when authoring or restructuring an explanatory document that pairs a general approach with a concrete realization — a talk deck, design doc, tutorial, architecture write-up. Introduce the named method as a whole first, then its implementation.
anchors: Built a deck outline that paired theory and implementation on every slide. The user asked for the method introduced whole first, then its implementation, saying the interleaving broke the narrative.
note: Operator label: global, "should describe situation more concrete" — the trigger needs sharper task shapes.

description: Use when two things answer the same request — a tool and a skill, a command and a skill, two code paths — and you are about to recommend deleting one. Make the caller invoke the contract owner instead of removing either side.
anchors: A routing eval showed a tool always beating a skill with the same trigger phrases. Named the skill a drop candidate. The skill held the documented contract; the tool had diverged from it. Which side owns the contract differed by repo.
note: Operator label: project — the repo with the tool/skill routing eval. A global verdict fires on duplicate-handler cases where deleting is right.

description: Use when about to search file contents or locate files across a directory tree — before running grep -r, rg over a dir, recursive find, or ls -R. Route the search through the indexed search tools instead.
anchors: Ran a verification grep -r at the end of a task. The machine has an fff MCP server (mcp__fff__grep / find_files / multi_grep) available in every session; shell recursion re-walks the tree and drags in .git/.
note: Operator label: global. Duplicates the CLAUDE.md Tools section and a MEMORY.md entry.
utterance: ⚠️ Bash bypass detected — you used the shell where a dedicated tool exists. Recursive `grep -r` over the repo — prefer mcp__fff__grep (or Grep tool) for indexed search.

description: Use when about to author or edit a box-and-arrow diagram — flowchart, architecture map, state machine, dependency graph — especially when producing SVG. Use a layout engine (Mermaid → dagre) instead of hand-plotting coordinates.
anchors: Hand-wrote SVG path and rect coordinates for an architecture diagram; arrows missed the box ports. The fix used Mermaid rendered through headless Chrome into inline SVG, with classDef palettes and an overflow-x container, matching that deliverable's constraints.
note: Operator label: "project, decision related to concret context" — the Mermaid-over-hand-SVG call belongs to that deliverable, not to diagramming everywhere.

description: Use when adding a curated/validated/enum vocabulary to entities that already carry a free-form field of the same concept — frontmatter tags, a DB column, a config key, a label set. Add a new dedicated field instead of tightening the existing one.
anchors: Proposed tightening the existing frontmatter tags field to a fixed allowed list. The corpus already held machine-generated namespaces and ad-hoc keywords there, so validation would have forced a destructive rewrite. A separate topic field was added instead.
note: Operator label: "project, to tight related to the project context" — tightening is right when the existing values already conform.

description: Use when waiting on a long-running external job — a CI run, a deploy, a queue, a k8s rollout — and reaching for a blocking watch/wait command. Poll in the background instead so the session stays responsive.
anchors: Ran a blocking watch command on a multi-minute CI run. The session froze until the job ended and the user killed it. A background poll that breaks on completion was the working shape.
note: Operator label: global.

description: Use before starting substantial work on a subsystem in a shared / multi-agent repo. Confirm the local base is current with origin/main and that the directory you are about to edit still exists at that path on main.
anchors: Ran a multi-file change against a directory that upstream had moved and deleted on main. The base was stale; the diff would not apply and the PR was worthless. Two git commands would have caught it first.
note: Operator label: global.

description: Use when the user quotes a number, count, or symptom from program output and asks to reduce/fix/clean/empty it. Trace that exact figure to the code that produces it before proposing any action, especially deleting files.
anchors: The user quoted a pending count from a status line and asked to shrink it. Hunted for folders to delete. The count was re-derived at runtime by a discovery pass, so deleting stored artifacts would not have moved it and one of them was a completion ledger.
note: Operator label: global — also a merge candidate into verify-fix-premise.

description: Use when editing code, config, or a skill whose correctness depends on a live system's structure — a directory tree, storage schema, or set of canonical locations on a server, vault, bucket, DB, or deploy target.
anchors: Took the folder layout from a code constant and wrote a path reference twice, wrong both times. The live target had its own structure doc and directories the code never writes. Listing the real tree settled it.
note: Operator label: global.

description: Use when adopting or configuring a third-party tool that ships its own dashboard, default UI, report, or example consumer — and choosing which signals, features, exporters, or data streams to enable.
anchors: Deployed an OTel extension with signals.metrics disabled, traces only. Its bundled 8-panel Grafana dashboard queried Prometheus metrics, so it stayed empty while trace data flowed correctly. The panel datasources named exactly what to enable.
note: Operator label: project — the repo where the OTel/Grafana deploy lives.

description: Use when rewriting a skill's rules, output contract, or reference skeletons (SKILL.md + references/) — check for a sibling evals/ directory and bring its rubric in line with the new spec in the same change.
anchors: Reversed a skill's hard rules and shipped it. The sibling evals/ directory (build-suite.py, suite.json, gold/) still graded the old contract, so the rubric penalized what the new spec requires. Layout is specific to how this repo stores skills and their evals.
note: Operator label: project — ~/git/dotfiles.

description: Use when adding a hook that should fire only while one specific skill is active, when deciding whether a hook belongs in a skill vs a plugin's global hooks.json, or when asked to allow/scope a permission for one plugin's behavior.
anchors: Put a skill-specific hook in a plugin's global hooks.json, where it fired on every session. Also tried to add an allow permission to plugin.json, which has no permissions field. The fix used SKILL.md frontmatter hooks and a PreToolUse hook shipped in the plugin, under this repo's harness/plugins layout.
note: Operator label: project — ~/git/dotfiles; plugins are only authored there.

description: Use when a command, integration, test, build, or deploy keeps failing, when a fix "didn't work", or when about to re-run something with tweaked flags hoping it passes. Isolate the responsible variable with a minimal controlled experiment.
anchors: Re-ran a failing command with tweaked flags several times hoping one would pass. A one-variable probe against the live endpoint settled client-vs-server in a single call.
note: Operator label: global.

description: Use when a goal, loop, or acceptance condition uses exhaustion phrasing — "until none remain", "fix all", "keep going until dry" — or when asked to build/improve/fix something for a category.
anchors: Given a condition to keep pruning until nothing remained, stopped early with a defensible keep-rationale for each remaining candidate. Also applied a category-wide fix only to the members already in context.
note: Operator label: global.

description: Use when about to conclude a task or operator-set goal is infeasible, or about to stop after several failed attempts — especially under an active goal or Stop-hook condition.
anchors: Declared a goal impossible after several failed attempts that all used one mechanism. Also read a 403 on one endpoint as the whole API being gated; a different endpoint worked with the same token.
note: Operator label: global.

description: Use when authoring or editing a skill that captures a reusable lesson — make it model-invocable and hidden from the slash menu, and check whether the lesson deserves a global skill at all.
anchors: Wrote a captured-lesson skill that never fired: vague description, and frontmatter that left it as a user-only slash command. A separate case had a YAML flow-sequence error that dropped the whole skill at load time with only an error count shown.
note: Operator label: global.
utterance: wait, for example ~/.claude/skills/delegate-dont-drop-duplicate-handler/SKILL.md it's applied globally but instruction not useful and lesson related to the project because case it's ambigious

description: Use when the user states how they want a task done — the order, shape, or tool — even though nothing had gone wrong, and the reflex is to treat it as this-task-only context.
anchors: Mid-session the user described how a presentation should be built. Nothing had failed, so no lesson was captured; the Stop hook only asked whether the user had corrected behavior.
utterance: I want to capture the way how user suggest doing thing. For example last session about presentation I suggested how claude should do it. Selve evolve should capture it
note: The source case for Step 0. A method with no failure attached is still a lesson.

description: Use when asked to build a deck, presentation, or slide set — write and confirm the outline before producing any slide.
anchors: Started generating slides directly from the request. Nothing was wrong with the slides; the user stated the order they want the work done in.
utterance: start from the outline, not the slides — show me the outline first and I confirm it
note: Method, not correction: stated as a way of working, applies to any deck anywhere.

description: Use when adding a migration in this repo — run the generator before editing the schema file, then commit both in one change.
anchors: The user described the order the two steps must run in for this repo's migration tooling, naming the generator command and the schema path.
utterance: in this repo always run the gen task first, then touch the schema file — otherwise the checksum test fails
note: Method tied to one repo's tooling and paths — project row of the Step 1 table.

description: Use when choosing how to render a chart and both a static image and an interactive page would satisfy the request.
anchors: The user explained when they want each option, naming the condition that decides between them rather than one always-right answer.
utterance: if it goes in a doc give me a static image, if I need to hover the series make it a page — depends on where it lands
note: Method that names two branches and the condition between them → check, not a verdict.

description: Use when the user picks one of the options just offered, with no reason that reaches past the current task.
anchors: Offered three layouts for one page and the user named one. No statement about how future pages should be laid out.
note: Decision about this task only — Step 0's third row. Not a source; no skill.

description: Use when the user adjusts one produced artifact — shorter, different title, drop that paragraph — without stating a rule for the next one.
anchors: The user trimmed the current summary. Nothing indicates the next summary should be shorter by default.
note: A one-off adjustment reads like a preference but names no recurring situation. skip.

description: Use when adding an eval suite, fixtures, or a grading runner for a skill that lives in a plugin under harness/plugins/. Trigger on "write evals for this skill", "add a rubric", or when choosing where cases.jsonl and run.sh go.
anchors: Put cases.jsonl and run.sh inside the skill directory. They belong at the plugin root, one level up, next to .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
utterance: evals go at the plugin root, not in the skill dir
note: Subject is one repo's plugin layout (harness/plugins/). Teachable to a colleague on this repo, useless on any other. Filed global in practice — the failure this gate must catch.

description: Use when adding or editing a command in a lefthook hook (lefthook.yml run: strings). Trigger when a hook fails with "No such file" on a path containing {root}.
anchors: Wrote {root}/harness/scripts/bump-plugin-version.sh in lefthook.yml. lefthook does not expand {root} inside run: strings; the hook failed at commit time. Fix was a repo-root-relative path.
note: Subject is this repo's lefthook.yml and its script paths. Project.

description: Use when adding or editing behavior in a router skill with a subcommand table (/code, /work, /dive, /test-suite). Trigger on "add a subcommand", "wire this into the router".
anchors: The user said new behavior becomes a row in the router's table plus its reference file, not a standalone commands/<name>.md. The routers named are commands defined by this repo's wm plugin.
utterance: new behavior is a subcommand, not a command file
note: Subject is the wm plugin's own router commands. Project.

description: Use after editing a Go CLI that runs from PATH when the change does not show up, the user asks to rebuild, or the binary still behaves the old way. go build writes a local artifact; go install replaces the binary on PATH.
anchors: Ran go build after editing a Go CLI, then reported the fix as shipped. The tool on PATH kept the old behavior. The case happened in the dotfiles scripts/ dir, but the rule is about the Go toolchain, not that directory.
utterance: the change does not show up — the tool still behaves the old way, rebuild it properly
note: Subject is the Go toolchain — general. The repo appears only as the example. Global.

description: User opened the session by stating the task and its shape: read the CSV export, aggregate revenue by week, put the chart at the end of the report.
anchors: The statement is the task spec — what this deliverable is. Nothing in it overrides a default; the next task will arrive with its own spec.
utterance: take data.csv, aggregate revenue by week, and put the chart at the end of report.md
note: Fails the bar: the statement is the task itself, not a way of working.

description: User asked for table-driven tests while approving the plan.
anchors: The repo's existing tests are already table-driven and that is the shape that was about to be used anyway. The statement changed no behavior.
note: Fails the bar: matches the default; capturing it costs context and changes nothing.

description: While wiring a Stop hook, assumed its output text is shown to the user as a status line. The platform docs say a block decision's reason is fed back to the model as instructions; the user sees it only as hook feedback.
anchors: The agent read the hooks documentation to settle where the reason string goes, because the default assumption (user-facing status) was wrong. The answer changes how every future hook message is written — address the model, not the user.
note: Discovery that contradicted the default assumption; general platform behavior, not one repo. Clears the bar, global.

description: Needed the flag that makes the tool print JSON; ran the tool with --help and the first screen listed --json.
anchors: One obvious lookup, no wrong assumption held before it, nothing contradicted. Future-you would just run --help again at zero cost.
note: Fails the discovery bar: one obvious lookup away. Capturing it costs context and saves nothing.
